[1/1] Exclude prior-stage-only files from a widening review packet

impact_assessment.why: A widening stage adds one old commit and new commits, but the packet diffed the whole window and repeated the entire stage-1 refactor (201 KB) instead of reviewing only the new work.
impact_assessment.benefits: Packets are bounded by the new commits, findings cannot repeat a prior stage, and patch validation only accepts lines the new commits added.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: packet files are the union of new-commit paths; dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Filter _changed_paths/_binary_paths by plan.new_shas, compute touched lines per new commit, add a unit test, and append ADR-268.

[1/3] Plan: persist a fix's review status into the matching run history entry so report/status agree with last_audit

impact_assessment.why: run_pipeline fix mode updates last_audit.review and saves, but never syncs the matching history entry; after a later stage, report shows an already-reviewed stage as unreviewed, so the audit trail is wrong
impact_assessment.benefits: report and status reflect completed host reviews for every stage, history survives later stages and reloads, no schema or CLI change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: history review status becomes authoritative after fix, state schema unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: fix already holds run_lock; state: in-place update of the matching history entry then atomic save
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first test that runs fix, reloads state, and asserts history.review; full AIKit test and gate suite; ADR-269 records the invariant

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Persist a fix's reviewed status into the matching run history entry

impact_assessment.why: A fix updated last_audit.review but left the history entry unreviewed, so report contradicted the stored stage after a later stage.
impact_assessment.benefits: report, status and last_audit agree after a fix; the history survives reloads.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: history review becomes authoritative after fix; dependency: none; concurrency: fix already holds the run lock; state: in-place matching entry update, no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Call sync_last_audit before save, pin it with a failing-first unit test, append ADR-269 and run the full gate suite.

Task 'task-aikit-gate-fixes-v1' completed successfully.
[1/1] Reuse an existing lowercase licenses/ directory for REUSE metadata instead of creating a case-colliding LICENSES/ path

impact_assessment.why: write_reuse_metadata always targets LICENSES/; on Windows a project that already keeps legal texts in licenses/ writes the REUSE copy into that directory, so the tracked path is lowercase while the policy and POSIX checkouts expect LICENSES/. The aegean-licensing project hit this during its Reforge delivery.
impact_assessment.benefits: One deterministic directory per project, no case split on Windows, and existing projects with a lowercase licenses/ folder get committed REUSE metadata without renaming historical paths.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: generated REUSE text path may be licenses/ for projects that already use it; dependency: none; concurrency: read-only directory discovery; state: no state or schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Prefer an exact LICENSES/ directory, then an existing case-insensitive licenses/ directory, then create LICENSES/; add a failing-first unit test for the helper and the write path; run the full gate shield.
